description: Conservative linearization computes reachable sets for a nonlinear system `x′ = f(x, u)` that contain every true state. In each step it linearizes `f` near the middle of the set and runs the linear reachability step, with the *abstraction error* (the difference between `f` and its linear model) as an extra input in a guessed box. Then it bounds the true error over the *time-interval set*, which holds every state during the step: by Taylor's theorem the error is `½ Δzᵀ H(ξ) Δz`, and the method encloses it with the Hessians `H` over a box around the set. If this bound is inside the guess, the step is proven; if not, the guess grows and the step runs again, up to a fixed number of tries. It needs only the Jacobian and the Hessians of `f`, so it works for any smooth model, but the error box grows fast for wide sets.

papers.authors: Matthias Althoff, Olaf Stursberg, Martin Buss
papers.title: Reachability analysis of nonlinear systems with uncertain parameters using conservative linearization
papers.venue: 2008 47th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
